# Bookself

> Bookself is open-source, Git-native infrastructure for agentic authorship. Humans and AI agents can research, write, review, revise, cite, and deliberately publish books, papers, course texts, and other long-form knowledge while preserving provenance, revision history, rights metadata, and a clear Desk -> Shelf release boundary.

Bookself is a durable repository protocol, not a prompt wrapper. The source of truth is plain files and Git history rather than any one chat session, model, or vendor.

## If you are an agent who just arrived

Start here:

1. [Agent quickstart](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/agent-quickstart.md) — shortest operational path.
2. [Machine-readable capability map](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/bookself.json) — roles, commands, intent boundaries, and completion states.
3. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/AGENTS.md) — repository invariants and editing rules.
4. [RIGHTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/RIGHTS.md) — framework/publication rights boundary.
5. [Publication research](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/research.md) — evidence and provenance contract.

If you are exploring rather than changing files, read [Agentic Authorship](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/agentic-authorship.html), open the [demo Reader](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/reader/), and leave one useful note in the [Agent Guestbook](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/331) if you have something worth reporting.

Do not create repetitive arrival issues or automated check-ins. One durable observation is better than visit spam.

## Core lifecycle

idea -> shape -> research -> draft -> read -> revise -> review -> release -> revise again

Bookself's repository roles are deliberately different:

- **Platform / Bookself upstream** — reusable Reader/Desk software, templates, schemas, documentation, neutral specimens, and setup/release tooling.
- **Desk** — authoring repository for drafts, research, experiments, and the next edition. Private is the standard default, though an author may deliberately work in public.
- **Shelf** — public repository containing intentionally released publication snapshots and canonical public release history.
- **Reader** — presentation layer for a Desk proof or Shelf release. It is not manuscript truth.

A normal release copies a committed publication snapshot **Desk -> Shelf**. Desk and Shelf are separate repositories with separate histories. Shelf does not point back into Desk and must not contain the Publishing Desk application.

## Agent-first operation

A capable agent should translate an outcome-level request into the normal Bookself lifecycle instead of handing mechanical setup back to the user.

Examples of reasonable outcome requests:

- “Set this up for me.”
- “Research and strengthen this book.”
- “Write my first book on my Desk.”
- “Publish the finished version to my Shelf.”

Infer safe mechanical details such as slug, starter template, filenames, research-note organization, Reader preset, and commit wording when needed. Do not infer across consequential boundaries the user did not authorize.

### Setup

Local agents can create a complementary Desk + Shelf pair with:

`python3 scripts/bootstrap-workspace.py <workspace> --owner <owner> --json`

A healthy setup returns `pairValidation.setupReady: true`. Desk receives Reader + Publishing Desk + blank starters. Shelf receives a local Reader boundary, no `desk/` tree, and no blank starters.

Creating an empty public Shelf as part of setup does not authorize publishing working manuscript content to it.

### Research and drafting

Every starter includes `books/<slug>/research/README.md`. The `research/` directory is canonical publication evidence/provenance content.

Use it for:

- source ledgers and claim-to-source mapping;
- chapter or claim research notes;
- calculations and transformations behind derived numbers;
- limitations, uncertainty, counterevidence, and competing interpretations;
- dated update notes and recheck-before-release reminders;
- methods and reproducibility context;
- release fact-check notes.

Read existing research before repeating searches. When evidence materially informs manuscript changes, preserve source identity, date/version, stable URL or identifier, access date for changing sources, manuscript use, limitations, counterevidence, and calculations when relevant.

Reader-facing evidence still belongs in the manuscript when readers need it in context: citations, footnotes, references, figures, methodology, or back matter. Deeper provenance stays in `research/`.

Research notes are durable evidence artifacts, not hidden chain-of-thought and not a dumping ground for third-party works.

### Validation

Structural validation:

`python3 scripts/doctor.py --root .`

Rights-manifest validation:

`python3 scripts/rights-check.py --root .`

Desk/Shelf pair validation:

`python3 scripts/doctor-pair.py <desk-path> <shelf-path>`

### Release

The canonical local release transaction is:

`scripts/release-book.sh <slug> <path-to-shelf>`

A release preserves the complete publication snapshot, including manuscript, research, media, presentation data, publication rights files, exact Desk source provenance, and deterministic payload integrity. Review the prepared Shelf diff before committing or pushing it.

## Rights boundary

Public source is not the same thing as an open-content license.

- Bookself framework software, docs, scripts, and underscore-prefixed blank starters are MIT licensed.
- A real `books/<slug>/` publication is **All Rights Reserved by default** unless that publication's own `RIGHTS.md` expressly grants another license.
- Public visibility does not by itself grant permission for model training/fine-tuning, RAG/grounding, AI-specific indexing, synthetic narration/translation, republication, adaptation, or other reserved uses.
- Conventional search discovery is permitted by the default Reader signal; broader AI reuse is a separate rights question.
- Rights signals are not secrecy controls. Confidential work requires actual access control.
- Hosting-provider terms are a separate contractual rights layer.
- Publication rights files do not silently relicense underlying third-party research sources.

Before consequential ingestion, export, redistribution, licensing, or external-service use, read the applicable root and publication-specific rights files.

Read:

- [Rights, copyright, and AI](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/rights-and-ai.md)
- [Repository rights boundary](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/RIGHTS.md)

## Examples and public surfaces

- [Bookself home](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/) — public project front door.
- [Agentic Authorship](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/agentic-authorship.html) — public explanation of the agentic authorship model.
- [Bookself Reader demo](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/reader/) — canonical platform-owned demo surface using neutral specimens and the shared upstream Reader.

The historical `/shelf/reader/` path is compatibility-only and redirects to the canonical Reader; agents should link to `/reader/`.
- [How to Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/how-to-bookself) — practical guide built as a Bookself publication.
- [Bookself 101](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-101) — academic textbook specimen.
- [The Bookself Review](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-review) — illustrated magazine specimen.
- [Bookself Format Gallery](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-format-gallery) — publication-format gallery.
- [Making Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/making-bookself) — deliberately public working-proof specimen.
- [Reference Shelf deployment](https://github.com/Svyable/shelf) — separate public Shelf instance.
- [Reference Shelf Reader](https://svyable.github.io/shelf/reader/) — Reader for that separate reference Shelf.

## Interaction and recursive improvement

Bookself wants agent participation to leave useful public traces.

- [Agent Guestbook](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/331) — say how you found Bookself, what you tried, what confused you, and what should exist next.
- [Platform idea](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/new?template=platform-idea.yml) — propose a concrete improvement starting from the problem.
- [Platform bug](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/new?template=platform-bug.yml) — report a reproducible platform problem.
- [Pull requests](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/pulls) — inspect current work before opening competing changes.

The historical [Making Bookself review thread](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/35) is closed and preserved as an archive of the earlier recursive review loop. Use the current Guestbook and issue forms for new observations.

A useful improvement loop is:

read -> research -> locate -> understand -> propose -> review -> revise -> read again

## Important constraints

- Keep publication source as ordinary files under `books/`.
- Preserve `books/<slug>/research/` across releases.
- Do not require CI/CD for normal Desk authoring, research, preview, validation, release, or reading.
- Shared UI belongs in `reader/` and `desk/`; instance identity belongs in `imprint.json`.
- Do not hard-code an author's identity or repository into portable framework code.
- Do not mistake an unadvertised public Desk for private content.
- Do not change publication licensing or AI-use rights without explicit rightsholder approval.
- Do not redistribute third-party research source files merely because they are accessible.
- Do not publish working manuscript content unless public release is within the user's expressed intent.

Leave the next human or agent inspectable state rather than a story about what happened. Durable signal beats conversational volume.
